newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Bank of England joins Kong Kong 97 souvenir frenzy.
newsitem.headline: Bank of England joins Kong Kong 97 souvenir frenzy.

text.p: The Bank of England will soon jostle for space with peddlers of souvenir t-shirts, pens, stamps and watches as it tries to cash in on Britain's return of Hong Kong to China on July 1.
The bank, in a rare change to its note design, has printed 500,000 five pound sterling notes numbered with a "HK97" prefix, the South China Morning Post said on Friday.
Single notes cost between HK$138 and HK$150 (US$17.85 and US$19.40), while an uncut sheet with 35 of the souvenir notes will cost HK$5,000 (US$646.80).
Those with unusual numbers like "HK97 000001" will be auctioned off -- starting at HK$50,000 (US$6,468).
They will go on sale at a four-day MoneyWorld Asia finance conference in Hong Kong next Friday.
Britain is handing its colony of 156 years back to China at midnight this June 30, and the territory has seen a flurry of souvenir items hit the streets to commemorate the flag change.
